anatomy.intro: The patent describes pale opalescent rosettes with thick spoon-shaped leaves and small pointed tips; this illustration does not identify the owned specimen.

parts.function: The thick spoon-shaped leaf forms part of the rosette.
parts.label: Fleshy blade

parts.function: The powdery coating gives the leaf a pale finish and can rub away to expose greener tissue.
parts.label: Glaucous surface

parts.function: A short point finishes the otherwise rounded leaf end.
parts.label: Small pointed tip

parts.function: Closely packed developing leaves occupy the rosette center.
parts.label: Young center

flowers.text: The patent records bell-shaped flowers with red-orange outer surfaces and yellow tips and interiors on a raised stem. Its spring and summer observations are not a flowering schedule for this indoor plant.

growth.note: Observe the actual plant over time; the breeder’s examples do not establish this specimen’s size or growth rate.

stages.text: Young leaves expand from the center into the thick spoon-shaped form.
stages.title: Develop the rosette

stages.text: The patent describes example rosettes about 15 cm wide four months after cutting; this is not a mature-size ceiling.
stages.title: Broaden the crown

stages.text: The breeder describes moderate offsetting; do not assume how many rooted plants are in the purchased container.
stages.title: Watch for offsets

habitat.text: 'Arctic Ice' is a cultivated hybrid selected in Vista, California. The patent names 'E1 IV' and 'Lila’s Surprise' as its parents; these cultivar names do not establish a species-level pedigree or a wild native range.

image.alt: Schematic pale Arctic Ice rosette with four numbered features: fleshy blade, glaucous surface, small pointed tip, and young center.
image.prompt: Create a square 1024px educational botanical illustration on warm ivory, clean pen-and-watercolor style matching a personal plant field guide. Subject Echeveria 'Arctic Ice': broad compact pale opalescent blue-green rosette, many thick smooth spoon-shaped leaves with rounded ends and tiny pointed tips, powdery glaucous surface, smaller tightly packed leaves at center. Slight overhead three-quarter view. No bumps or caruncles, no red rims, no flowers, no roots, no pots. Four numbered circular markers with thin clean noncrossing leaders: 1 to one broad fleshy outer leaf blade; 2 to matte powdery surface of another leaf; 3 to tiny pointed tip of a front leaf; 4 to young central leaves. Exactly numerals 1 2 3 4, no other text or title. Schematic cultivar reference, not a photograph of the owned specimen. Save generated project asset.

lookalikes.name: Echeveria elegans
lookalikes.text: Named as a commercial comparison in the patent, not a documented parent. Resemblance does not identify the owned plant.

lookalikes.name: Echeveria 'Perle von Nürnberg'
lookalikes.text: Also named as a commercial comparison, with variant spelling. Its purple coloring in reference photographs should not be transferred to Arctic Ice.

mature.text: The patent’s recorded plants had broad pale rosettes and moderate offsets. Its measured examples are not a mature-size ceiling; the owned plant’s dimensions remain unrecorded.

milestones.text: Owner reported acquisition at Home Depot and purchase of a six-inch blue-and-white ceramic pot; completed repot and current setup remain unrecorded.
milestones.title: Acquired at Home Depot

nameStory.text: Renee O’Connell made the February 2012 cross and selected the plant in March 2013. U.S. plant patent PP29,584 was issued August 7, 2018.
